title: Who wrote this line?
brief:
`config.txt` says `mode = unsafe` and production is on fire. Which commit did that? `git blame <file>` annotates every line with the commit that last touched it, who wrote it, and when. The `^` prefix marks lines from the very first commit.

Read the blame, find the line that flipped the mode, then fix it: set `mode` back to `safe` (keep `timeout = 60`; that change was a separate, innocent commit) and commit as "restore safe mode".

Blame is not for shaming; it is for finding the exact moment history changed its mind.

goals.label: The fix is committed as "restore safe mode"
Four commits: the fix sits on top

hints: git blame config.txt. Line 1's sha differs from line 2's: that commit is your culprit.
Edit config.txt to exactly: mode = safe / timeout = 60 (keep the timeout change; only the mode line was the crime).
Then git add config.txt and git commit -m "restore safe mode".
